assignedReviews.card_evidence: A type AB+ patient can receive any blood type right away without waiting for an exact match
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: Emergency transfusion matching is not identifying heart, blood, and blood vessels and how they work.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A type AB+ patient can receive any blood type right away
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: Transfusion matching is not the five body systems as a set.

copy.en:
Why is blood type AB+ special in emergencies?

A type AB+ patient can receive any blood type right away without waiting for an exact match — a big help in accidents!
copy.tl:
Bakit espesyal ang blood type AB+ sa emergency?

Ang pasyenteng may blood type AB+ ay pwedeng bigyan agad ng kahit anong blood type nang hindi naghihintay ng eksaktong tugma — malaking tulong sa mga aksidente!
copy.bis:
Nganong espesyal ang blood type AB+ sa emergency?

Ang pasyente nga adunay blood type AB+ mahatagan dayon og bisan unsang blood type nga wala maghulat sa eksaktong tugma — dakong tabang sa mga aksidente!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Type AB plasma has no anti-A or anti-B antibodies, making it the universal plasma donor
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: Plasma-donation matching is not identifying heart, blood, and blood vessels and how they work.

copy.en:
Why is type AB plasma special?

Type AB plasma has no anti-A or anti-B antibodies, making it the universal plasma donor — any patient can safely receive it!
copy.tl:
Bakit espesyal ang plasma ng type AB?

Walang anti-A o anti-B antibody ang plasma ng type AB, kaya ito ang universal plasma donor — kahit sinong pasyente ay ligtas tumanggap nito!
copy.bis:
Ngano espesyal ang plasma sa type AB?

Walay anti-A o anti-B antibody ang plasma sa type AB, mao nga kini ang universal plasma donor — bisan kinsang pasyente luwas modawat niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: AB has both A and B antigens but no antibodies, making it the universal recipient. O has no antigens but both antibodies, making it the universal donor
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: Universal donor versus recipient roles are typing, not identifying heart, blood, and blood vessels and how they work.

copy.en:
How are blood types AB and O opposites?

AB has both A and B antigens but no antibodies, making it the universal recipient. O has no antigens but both antibodies, making it the universal donor -- mirror images!
copy.tl:
Bakit magkasalungat ang blood type AB at O?

May A AT B antigen ang AB pero walang antibody, kaya universal recipient ito. Ang O naman ay walang antigen pero may anti-A at anti-B, kaya universal donor ito -- magkabaligtad sila!
copy.bis:
Nganong sukwahi ang blood type AB ug O?

Ang AB adunay A UG B antigen apan walay antibody, mao nga universal recipient. Ang O walay antigen apan adunay anti-A ug anti-B, mao nga universal donor -- baligtad sila!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Tropical rainforests, swamps, estuaries, mangrove forests, and coral reefs are types of ecosystems where living and nonliving things interact.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes ecosystem types and the interaction of living and nonliving things, but does not address the basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter) that G3-L-6 requires.

copy.en: Tropical rainforests, swamps, estuaries, mangrove forests, and coral reefs are types of ecosystems where living and nonliving things interact.
copy.tl: Ang tropical rainforests, swamps, estuaries, mangrove forests, at coral reefs ay mga uri ng ecosystem kung saan nag-uugnayan ang mga bagay na may buhay at walang buhay.
copy.bis: Ang tropical rainforests, swamps, estuaries, mangrove forests, ug coral reefs mga klase sa ecosystem diin ang mga buhi ug dili buhi nga butang mag-uban ug mag-interact.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A typhoon's strength is classified and categorized according to its wind speed!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the weather conditions according to a Public Storm Warning Signal issued by the Philippine Atmospheric, Geological and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA)
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that typhoon strength is categorized by wind speed, which is the underlying basis for PAGASA's Public Storm Warning Signals. However, it does not describe the specific weather conditions associated with any signal level, nor does it mention PAGASA or the warning signal system itself. It provides background knowledge but does not directly teach the competency.

copy.en: A typhoon's strength is classified and categorized according to its wind speed!
copy.tl: Ang lakas ng isang bagyo (typhoon) ay inuuri ayon sa bilis ng hangin nito!
copy.bis: Ang kusog sa usa ka bagyo (typhoon) giklasipikar sumala sa katulin sa hangin niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The eye of a typhoon is usually about 30 to 65 kilometers across.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe typical weather conditions before, during, and after a tropical cyclone
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the typical size of a typhoon's eye. It does not describe weather conditions before, during, or after a tropical cyclone, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The eye of a typhoon is usually about 30 to 65 kilometers across.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a dimension of a typhoon's eye, which is not one of the basic weather characteristics listed (air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, cloud cover). It shares the broad weather topic but does not teach identification of weather characteristics.

copy.en: The eye of a typhoon is usually about 30 to 65 kilometers across. That is a really big clear space!
copy.tl: Ang mata ng bagyo ay karaniwang mga 30 hanggang 65 kilometro ang lapad. Iyon ay napakalawak na malinaw na espasyo!
copy.bis: Ang mata sa bagyo kasagaran mga 30 ngadto sa 65 ka kilometro ang gilapdon. Kini dako kaayong klaro nga espasyo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sometimes the old eyewall gets replaced by a new one!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to explain: a. how typhoons develop, and b. why the Philippines is prone to typhoons
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a specific typhoon phenomenon (eyewall replacement cycle) but does not explain how typhoons develop or why the Philippines is prone to typhoons. It is only tangentially related to typhoon behavior.

copy.en:
Can a typhoon take a little break?

Sometimes the old eyewall gets replaced by a new one! The typhoon weakens for a while, then grows strong again.
copy.tl:
Pwede bang magpahinga ang bagyo nang sandali?

Minsan, ang lumang eyewall ay napapalitan ng bago! Humihina ang bagyo nang sandali, tapos lalakas ito ulit.
copy.bis:
Mahimo bang magpahulay ang bagyo gamay?

Usahay, ang daan nga eyewall mailisan ug bag-o! Mohuyang ang bagyo gamay, unya mokusog kini pag-usab.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The eyewall is the thick ring of clouds around the eye, and it holds the strongest winds and heaviest rain in the whole typhoon!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to explain: a. how typhoons develop, and b. why the Philippines is prone to typhoons
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a structural feature of a typhoon (the eyewall) but does not explain how typhoons develop or why the Philippines is prone to typhoons. It shares the typhoon topic but provides no direct instructional support for the competency's required explanations.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The eyewall is the thick ring of clouds around the eye, and it holds the strongest winds and heaviest rain in the whole typhoon!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe typical weather conditions before, during, and after a tropical cyclone
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes conditions during a typhoon (strongest winds and heaviest rain in the eyewall) but does not describe typical weather conditions before, during, and after a tropical cyclone as a sequence. It only touches on one aspect of the 'during' phase, so it does not directly support the full competency.

copy.en: The eyewall is the thick ring of clouds around the eye, and it holds the strongest winds and heaviest rain in the whole typhoon!
copy.tl: Ang eyewall ay ang makapal na singsing ng ulap sa paligid ng mata, at dito matatagpuan ang pinakamalakas na hangin at pinakamalakas na ulan sa buong bagyo!
copy.bis: Ang eyewall mao ang baga nga singsing sa panganod nga naglibot sa mata, ug dinhi makita ang pinakakusog nga hangin ug pinakakusog nga ulan sa tibuok bagyo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When a typhoon is very destructive and causes many deaths, PAGASA retires its name forever
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe some effects of weather disturbances that occur in or near the Philippines
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the retirement of typhoon names by PAGASA, not the effects of weather disturbances. It shares the typhoon topic but does not describe any effects of weather disturbances.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When a typhoon is very destructive and causes many deaths, PAGASA retires its name forever
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe typical weather conditions before, during, and after a tropical cyclone
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about naming conventions for destructive typhoons, not about typical weather conditions before, during, or after a tropical cyclone. It is only topically related.

copy.en: When a typhoon is very destructive and causes many deaths, PAGASA retires its name forever so it is never used again — like the name Yolanda!
copy.tl: Kapag napakasira ng isang bagyo at marami ang namatay, ire-retire ng PAGASA ang pangalan nito nang tuluyan — hindi na gagamitin muli, tulad ng pangalang Yolanda!
copy.bis: Kung ang usa ka bagyo grabe kaayo ug daghan ang namatay, i-retire sa PAGASA ang ngalan niini sa walay katapusan — dili na gamiton pag-usab, sama sa ngalang Yolanda!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Always prepare yours before a typhoon arrives.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: examine a local weather chart to make simple interpretations about the local weather and describe and practice safety precautions to use during poor or extreme weather conditions
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a go-bag as a typhoon preparedness item, which is a safety precaution for extreme weather. However, the competency requires examining a local weather chart to make simple interpretations about local weather, and the card does not address weather charts or interpretation at all. The go-bag content is only tangentially related to the safety-precautions portion of the competency, not direct instructional support for the stated skill.

copy.en: A go-bag holds emergency essentials like food, water, medicine, important documents, and a flashlight! Always prepare yours before a typhoon arrives.
copy.tl: Ang go-bag ay may mga emergency essentials tulad ng pagkain, tubig, gamot, mahalagang dokumento, at flashlight! Ihanda ito bago dumating ang bagyo.
copy.bis: Ang go-bag adunay mga emergency essentials sama sa pagkain, tubig, gamot, importante nga dokumento, ug flashlight! I-andam kini sa wala pa moabot ang bagyo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A typhoon has three main parts
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe typical weather conditions before, during, and after a tropical cyclone
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the structural parts of a typhoon (eye, eyewall, rainbands), but does not describe typical weather conditions before, during, or after a tropical cyclone. It shares the typhoon topic but does not directly support the competency's skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A typhoon has three main parts
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to explain: a. how typhoons develop, and b. why the Philippines is prone to typhoons
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the anatomy of a typhoon, not how typhoons develop or why the Philippines is prone to typhoons. It is related to the typhoon subject but does not provide the explanatory content required by the competency.

copy.en: A typhoon has three main parts: the calm eye at the center, the eyewall with the strongest winds, and the spiral rainbands carrying rain around the outside!
copy.tl: Ang isang bagyo ay may tatlong pangunahing bahagi: ang tahimik na mata sa gitna, ang eyewall na may pinakamalakas na hangin, at ang mga spiral rainbands na nagdadala ng ulan sa palibot!
copy.bis: Ang usa ka bagyo adunay tulo ka nag-unang bahin: ang malinawon nga mata sa tunga, ang eyewall nga adunay labing kusog nga hangin, ug ang mga spiral rainband nga nagdala sa ulan sa palibot!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A typhoon watch means danger is possible in 48 hours. A typhoon warning means danger is expected in 24 hours!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the weather conditions according to a Public Storm Warning Signal issued by the Philippine Atmospheric, Geological and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA)
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the difference between a typhoon watch and a typhoon warning, which are general alert terms. The competency specifically requires describing weather conditions according to a PAGASA Public Storm Warning Signal (e.g., Signal No. 1, 2, 3). The card does not mention PAGASA signal numbers or the associated weather conditions, so it only shares the broad typhoon-alert topic without directly supporting the competency.

copy.en: A typhoon watch means danger is possible in 48 hours. A typhoon warning means danger is expected in 24 hours!
copy.tl: Ang typhoon watch ay nangangahulugang posibleng may peligro sa loob ng 48 oras. Ang typhoon warning naman ay nangangahulugang may peligro sa loob ng 24 oras!
copy.bis: Ang typhoon watch nagpasabot nga posible ang peligro sulod sa 48 ka oras. Ang typhoon warning nagpasabot nga gilauman ang peligro sulod sa 24 ka oras!
